solution:
Let \(f(x)=\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x\)  ..... (I)
We have to prove that \(f(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}\)
Differentiate (I) w. r. t. x
\(\frac{d}{dx}[f(x)]=\frac{d}{dx}[\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x]\)
\(f'(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=0\)
\(f'(x)=0 \Rightarrow f(x)\) is a constant function.
Let \(f(x)=c\). For any value of \(x\), \(f(x)\) must be \(c\) only. So conveniently we can choose \(x=0\),
\(\therefore\) from (I) we get,
\(f(0)=\sin^{-1}(0)+\cos^{-1}(0)=0+\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow c=\frac{\pi}{2} \therefore f(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}\)
Hence, \(\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x=\frac{\pi}{2}\).

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\sin^{-1}(x^3)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\sin^{-1}(x^3)\right)\)
\(=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(x^3)^2}}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(x^3)\)
\(=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^6}}(3x^2)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{3x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^6}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cos^{-1}(2x^2-x)\)
Hence \(\cos y=2x^2-x\)   ... (I)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(-\sin y\cdot\frac{dy}{dx}=4x-1\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1-4x}{\sin y}=\frac{1-4x}{\sqrt{1-\cos^2 y}}\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1-4x}{\sqrt{1-x^2(2x-1)^2}}\)   ... from (I)
Alternate Method :
If \(y=\cos^{-1}(2x^2-x)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\cos^{-1}(2x^2-x)\right)\)
\(=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{1-(2x^2-x)^2}}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(2x^2-x)\)
\(=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{1-x^2(2x-1)^2}}\cdot(4x-1)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1-4x}{\sqrt{1-x^2(2x-1)^2}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\sin^{-1}(2^x)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\sin^{-1}(2^x)\right)\)
\(=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(2^x)^2}}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(2^x)\)
\(=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-2^{2x}}}(2^x\log 2)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2^x\log 2}{\sqrt{1-4^x}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cot^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^2}\right)=\tan^{-1}(x^2)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}(\tan^{-1}(x^2))\)
\(=\frac{1}{1+(x^2)^2}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(x^2)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2x}{1+x^4}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cos^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{2}}\right)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\cos^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{2}}\right)\right]\)
\(=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\left(\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{2}}\right)^2}}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}\left(\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{2}}\right)\)
\(=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\frac{1+x}{2}}}\times\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{2}}}\times\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{1+x}{2}\right)\)
\(=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{1-x}}\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\sqrt{1+x}}\times\frac{1}{2}\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1-x^2}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\sin^2(\sin^{-1}(x^2))\)
\(=[\sin(\sin^{-1}(x^2))]^2=(x^2)^2\)
\(\therefore y=x^4\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}(x^4)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=4x^3\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cos^{-1}(4\cos^3 x-3\cos x)\)
\(=\cos^{-1}(\cos 3x)\)
\(\therefore y=3x\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}(3x)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=3\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cos^{-1}[\sin(4^x)]\)
\(=\cos^{-1}\left[\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-4^x\right)\right]\)
\(\therefore y=\frac{\pi}{2}-4^x\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-4^x\right)=0-4^x\log 4\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=-4^x\log 4\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{1-\cos x}{2}}\right)\)
\(=\sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{2\sin^2\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}{2}}\right)\)
\(=\sin^{-1}\left[\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]\)
\(\therefore y=\frac{x}{2}\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{2}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1-\cos 3x}{\sin 3x}\right)\)
\(=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\sin^2\left(\frac{3x}{2}\right)}{2\sin\left(\frac{3x}{2}\right)\cos\left(\frac{3x}{2}\right)}\right)\)
\(=\tan^{-1}\left[\tan\left(\frac{3x}{2}\right)\right]\)
\(\therefore y=\frac{3x}{2}\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{3x}{2}\right)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{3}{2}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cot^{-1}\left(\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}\right)\)
\(=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\left[\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]^2}{\cos^2\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)-\sin^2\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\left[\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]^2}{\left[\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]\left[\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]}\right)\)
\(=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}{\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1+\tan\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}{1-\tan\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}\right)\) ....Divide Numerator & Denominator by \(\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\)
\(=\tan^{-1}\left[\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]\)
\(\therefore y=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{x}{2}\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{x}{2}\right)=0+\frac{1}{2}\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{2}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the book's printed solution writes \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\cos x+\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\cos x\) (the second term should be \(\sin x\)) and checks \(\frac{4}{3}+\frac{9}{13}=1\) (should be \(\frac{4}{13}\)). The printed final answer \(\frac{dy}{dx}=1\) is correct.]

Let \(y=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2\cos x+3\sin x}{\sqrt{13}}\right)\)
\(=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\cos x+\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\cos x\right)\)
Put \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}=\sin\alpha, \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}=\cos\alpha\)
Also, \(\sin^2\alpha+\cos^2\alpha=\frac{4}{3}+\frac{9}{13}=1\)
And \(\tan\alpha=\frac{2}{3} \therefore \alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}(\sin\alpha\cos x+\cos\alpha\sin x)\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}(\sin x\cos\alpha+\cos x\sin\alpha)\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}[\sin(x+\alpha)]\)
\(\therefore y=x+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[x+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\right]=1+0\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=1\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3\sin x^2+4\cos x^2}{5}\right)\)
\(=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\sin x^2+\frac{4}{5}\cos x^2\right)\)
Put \(\frac{3}{5}=\sin\alpha, \frac{4}{5}=\cos\alpha\)
Also, \(\sin^2\alpha+\cos^2\alpha=\frac{9}{25}+\frac{16}{25}=1\)
And \(\tan\alpha=\frac{3}{4} \therefore \alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}(\sin\alpha\sin x^2+\cos\alpha\cos x^2)\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}(\cos x^2\cos\alpha+\sin x^2\sin\alpha)\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}[\cos(x^2-\alpha)]\)
\(\therefore y=x^2-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[x^2-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\right]=2x-0\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=2x\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{a\cos x-b\sin x}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\right)=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\cos x-\frac{b}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\sin x\right)\)
Put \(\frac{a}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}=\sin\alpha, \frac{b}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}=\cos\alpha\)
Also, \(\sin^2\alpha+\cos^2\alpha=\frac{a^2}{a^2+b^2}+\frac{b^2}{a^2+b^2}=1\) And \(\tan\alpha=\frac{a}{b} \therefore \alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}(\sin\alpha\cos x-\cos\alpha\sin x)\)
But \(\sin(\alpha-x)=\sin\alpha\cos x-\cos\alpha\sin x\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}[\sin(\alpha-x)]\)
\(\therefore y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)-x\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)-x\right]=0-1\)   \(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=-1\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)\)
Put \(x=\tan\theta \therefore \theta=\tan^{-1}x\)
\(\therefore y=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2\tan\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}\right)\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}(\sin 2\theta)=2\theta\)
\(\therefore y=2\tan^{-1}x\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=2\frac{d}{dx}(\tan^{-1}x)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2}{1+x^2}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cos^{-1}\left(2x\sqrt{1-x^2}\right)\)
Put \(x=\sin\theta \therefore \theta=\sin^{-1}x\)
\(\therefore y=\cos^{-1}\left(2\sin\theta\sqrt{1-\sin^2\theta}\right)\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}\left(2\sin\theta\sqrt{\cos^2\theta}\right)\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}(2\sin\theta\cos\theta)=\cos^{-1}(\sin 2\theta)\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}\left[\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-2\theta\right)\right]=\frac{\pi}{2}-2\theta\)
\(\therefore y=\frac{\pi}{2}-2\sin^{-1}x\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-2\sin^{-1}x\right)\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=0-\frac{2\times 1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3x-4x^3}\right)\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}(3x-4x^3)\)
Put \(x=\sin\theta \therefore \theta=\sin^{-1}x\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}(3\sin\theta-4\sin^3\theta)\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}(\sin 3\theta)=3\theta\)
\(\therefore y=3\sin^{-1}x\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=3\frac{d}{dx}(\sin^{-1}x)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the book's printed solution writes \(\frac{2\tan\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}\) where \(\tan 2\theta\) requires \(1-\tan^2\theta\), and its printed final answer \(\frac{2e^x}{1-e^{2x}}\) contradicts its own preceding step \(\frac{2}{1+(e^x)^2}\). The correct answer is \(\frac{2e^x}{1+e^{2x}}\).]

Let \(y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2e^x}{1-e^{2x}}\right)\)
Put \(e^x=\tan\theta \therefore \theta=\tan^{-1}(e^x)\)
\(y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\tan\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}\right)\)
\(y=\tan^{-1}(\tan 2\theta)=2\theta\)
\(\therefore y=2\tan^{-1}(e^x)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=2\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}(e^x)\right]\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2}{1+(e^x)^2}\frac{d}{dx}(e^x)=\frac{2e^x}{1-e^{2x}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1-9x^2}{1+9x^2}\right)\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1-(3x)^2}{1+(3x)^2}\right)\)
Put \(3x=\tan\theta \therefore \theta=\tan^{-1}(3x)\)
\(\therefore y=\cos^{-1}\left[\frac{1-\tan^2\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}\right]\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}(\cos 2\theta)=2\theta\)
\(y=2\tan^{-1}(3x)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=2\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}(3x)\right]\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2}{1+(3x)^2}\frac{d}{dx}(3x)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{6}{1+9x^2}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2^x-2^{-x}}{2^x+2^{-x}}\right)\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2^x(2^x-2^{-x})}{2^x(2^x+2^{-x})}\right)\)   ... [Multiply & Devide by \(2^x\)]
\(y=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2^{2x}-1}{2^{2x}+1}\right)=\cos^{-1}\left[-\frac{1-(2^x)^2}{1+(2^x)^2}\right]\)
Put \(2^x=\tan\theta \therefore \theta=\tan^{-1}(2^x)\)
\(\therefore y=\cos^{-1}\left[-\frac{1-\tan^2\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}\right]=\cos^{-1}[-\cos 2\theta]\)
\(y=\cos^{-1}[\cos(\pi-2\theta)]=\pi-2\theta\)
\(y=\pi-2\tan^{-1}(2^x)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\pi-2\tan^{-1}(2^x)\right]\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=0-\frac{2}{1+(2^x)^2}\frac{d}{dx}(2^x)=-\frac{2\cdot 2^x\cdot\log 2}{1+2^{2x}}\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{2^{x+1}\log 2}{1+2^{2x}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\tan^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{3-x}{3+x}}\right)\)
Put \(x=3\cos 2\theta \therefore \theta=\frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)\)
\(\therefore y=\tan^{-1}\left[\sqrt{\frac{3-3\cos 2\theta}{3+3\cos 2\theta}}\right]=\tan^{-1}\left[\sqrt{\frac{3(1-\cos 2\theta)}{3(1+\cos 2\theta)}}\right]=\tan^{-1}\left[\sqrt{\frac{2\sin^2\theta}{2\cos^2\theta}}\right]\)
\(y=\tan^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\tan^2\theta}\right)=\tan^{-1}(\tan\theta)\)
\(y=\theta=\frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}\left[\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)\right]\)
\(=\frac{1}{2}\left[-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)^2}}\right]\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)=-\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{9-x^2}{9}}}\times\frac{1}{3}\)
\(=-\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{\frac{\sqrt{9-x^2}}{3}}\times\frac{1}{3}\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{9-x^2}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5\sqrt{1-x^2}-12x}{13}\right)\)
Put \(x=\sin\theta \therefore \theta=\sin^{-1}x\)
\(\therefore y=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5\sqrt{1-\sin^2\theta}-12\sin\theta}{13}\right)=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5\sqrt{\cos^2\theta}-12\sin\theta}{13}\right)=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5\cos\theta-12\sin\theta}{13}\right)\)
\(\therefore y=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\cos\theta-\frac{12}{13}\sin\theta\right)\)
Put \(\frac{5}{13}=\sin\alpha, \frac{12}{13}=\cos\alpha\)
Also, \(\sin^2\alpha+\cos^2\alpha=\frac{25}{169}+\frac{144}{169}=1\)
And \(\tan\alpha=\frac{5}{12} \therefore \alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)\)
\(y=\sin^{-1}(\sin\alpha\cos\theta-\cos\alpha\sin\theta)=\sin^{-1}[\sin(\alpha-\theta)]=(\alpha-\theta)\)
\(\therefore y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)-\sin^{-1}x\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)-\sin^{-1}x\right]=0-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the book's printed final answer carries a spurious minus sign, \(-\frac{2^{x+1}\log 2}{1+4^x}\). Every preceding step is positive and the derivative of \(2\tan^{-1}(2^x)\) cannot be negative; the correct answer is \(\frac{2^{x+1}\log 2}{1+4^x}\). The minus is genuine in part (vi) on the same page, where \(y=\pi-2\tan^{-1}(2^x)\).]

Let \(y=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2^{x+1}}{1+4^x}\right)=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2\cdot 2^x}{1+(2^x)^2}\right)\)
Put \(2^x=\tan\theta \therefore \theta=\tan^{-1}(2^x)\)
\(\therefore y=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2\tan\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}\right)=\sin^{-1}(\sin 2\theta)=2\theta=2\tan^{-1}(2^x)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=2\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}(2^x)\right]=\frac{2}{1+(2^x)^2}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(2^x)=\frac{2}{1+2^{2x}}(2^x\cdot\log 2)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{2^{x+1}\log 2}{1+4^x}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4x}{1+21x^2}\right)\)
\(=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{7x-3x}{1+(7x)(3x)}\right)\)
\(y=\tan^{-1}(7x)-\tan^{-1}(3x)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}(7x)-\tan^{-1}(3x)\right]\)
\(=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}(7x)\right]-\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}(3x)\right]\)
\(=\frac{1}{1+(7x)^2}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(7x)-\frac{1}{1+(3x)^2}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(3x)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{7}{1+49x^2}-\frac{3}{1+9x^2}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{7x}{1-12x^2}\right)\)
\(=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3x+4x}{1-(3x)(4x)}\right)\)
\(y=\tan^{-1}(3x)+\tan^{-1}(4x)\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}(3x)+\tan^{-1}(4x)\right]\)
\(=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}(3x)\right]+\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}(4x)\right]\)
\(=\frac{1}{1+(3x)^2}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(3x)+\frac{1}{1+(4x)^2}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(4x)\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{3}{1+9x^2}+\frac{4}{1+16x^2}\)

context: Differentiate the following w. r. t. x.
solution:
Let \(y=\cot^{-1}\left(\frac{b\sin x-a\cos x}{a\sin x+b\cos x}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{a\sin x+b\cos x}{b\sin x-a\cos x}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\frac{a}{b}+\cot x}{1-\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)(\cot x)}\right)\)
\(=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)+\tan^{-1}(\cot x)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)+\tan^{-1}\left[\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)\right]\)
\(y=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)+\frac{\pi}{2}-x\)
Differentiate w. r. t. x
\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)+\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right]\)
\(=\frac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)\right]+\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\frac{d}{dx}(x)\)
\(=0+0-1\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx}=-1\)
